subject: Wire instructions + VAT treatment for EUR payout on USD invoice
messages:
From: Simon Lester <simon.lester@acmedevices.com>

Cc: Acme Accounts <accounts.payable@acmedevices.com>
Date: 2028-10-01 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Payment routing question — invoice #INV-7789 (USD) / payout EUR

Hi Soojin,

We're ready to settle invoice INV-7789 (USD-denominated) but want to pay in EUR to our EU entity to avoid internal FX on our side. Can you confirm: 1) whether you accept EUR credit to Redwood's EU entity and the exact wire template we should use; 2) guidance on intermediary bank fees — do you require OUR (sender pays) or will you accept SHA (shared) and invoice any shortfalls back to us? Also, our AP team asks whether Redwood can provide a short note confirming VAT reverse-charge eligibility (we're a VAT-registered German entity, VAT ID DE123456789).

Appreciate a quick template we can hand to our bank.

Thanks,
Simon
Simon Lester
Head of Finance Operations
Acme Devices
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Simon Lester <simon.lester@acmedevices.com>
Cc: Acme Accounts <accounts.payable@acmedevices.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-01 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Payment routing question — invoice #INV-7789 (USD) / payout EUR

Hi Simon,

Thanks — quick response below and attaching a wire template (PDF) and our VAT reverse-charge guidance. High-level summary:

- We can accept EUR credit to Redwood EU (Redwood Inference Limited, DE branch) — see account block in the template.
- Preferred charge instruction: SHA (shared) is standard and avoids the payer needing to chase intermediate banks. If your bank insists on OUR, please confirm; we may ask Treasury to absorb the variable intermediate fees or net them depending on deal terms.
- Intermediary fees: typical corridors (USD->EUR via US correspondent) often incur one or two intermediary charges (USD 15-35 each). If SHA, the beneficiary (Redwood EU) will see the net amount after intermediaries; we will reconcile and issue a one-time debit/credit if the fee materially exceeds expectations.
- VAT: to apply reverse-charge, we need your EU VAT ID on the invoice (you already provided) and a short statement on our invoice such as: "VAT reverse-charge applies under Article 44/196 of the VAT Directive — recipient liable." We can add this line on the final invoice; I attached guidance.

Wire template highlights (in the PDF): account name, IBAN, SWIFT/BIC, bank name and address, reference (Invoice INV-7789 / PO 3321), and instruct your bank to include the reference in the MT103/SEPA field. For non-SEPA flows (USD correspondent hops), include the intermediary tag: /CHRG/ SHA or OUR — choose SHA unless instructed otherwise.

I'll loop in Finance (Laura, Ben) to confirm how we will handle any big intermediary fee variance relative to the invoice.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Head of Partner Payments (Europe)
Redwood Inference
Attachments: wire_template_acme.pdf; vat_reverse_charge_guidance.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-02 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Payment routing question — invoice #INV-7789 (USD) / payout EUR

Soojin / Laura — quick internal note from Finance:

- We prefer SHA for external payers. That avoids disputes and extra operational work.
- Policy: if intermediary fees reduce the payment by more than EUR 25 compared to invoice amount, Finance will either request a one-off top-up from the payer or apply a small reconciliation charge on the next invoice depending on client's preference.
- For large recurring clients we can make an exception and accept OUR, but we need a signed payment SLA addendum (handled by Marissa).

If Acme confirms SHA, we should provide a clean confirmation email they can share with their bank.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Manager, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

--- end payment block ---

If you see intermediaries remove any funds, send us the MT103 or a remittance screenshot and we'll reconcile.

Regards,
